# PART II — ENGINEERING DEEP-DIVE: TWENTY SYSTEMS AND THEIR INTERCONNECTIONS

## System A — Intelligence, inference, context, memory and epistemic honesty
The model is a reasoning resource, not the source of authorization. Separate user natural-language interpretation from deterministic executors. The mobile app first checks known low-risk local intents and explicit command aliases. More complex requests flow through a provider-neutral model router that can select a configured remote LLM, a user-installed on-device LLM, or a deterministic fallback. Build an intent classifier with labels, entities, language, target device, confidence band, required clarification and expected effects. Add a policy engine that approves tools based on user grants and device capability scopes, not model enthusiasm. Use schema validation at every boundary. Limit number of chained tool steps, time, money spent on inference, and maximum data transferred. If one action fails, report partial work and stop dependent actions unless retry is safe. Context management must keep the active user request, recent conversation, verified tool outcomes, explicitly opted-in memory, and selected document references separately typed. Do not turn an assistant guess into personal memory. Provide memory explainability: "You told me this in a previous approved session" and a review/delete control. Automatic summaries must preserve uncertainty and source dates; facts about external conditions require live verification when time-sensitive. Train/evaluate not merely on polished phrases but on tool refusal, ambiguous target, denied permission, unavailable model, changing device, mistaken identity, multilingual commands, and adversarial untrusted text. Optimize truthful and graceful responses over performative omniscience.

## System B — Audio capture, speech intelligence, and phone-speaker response
Implement Android AudioRecord or supported speech recognizer adapters behind an interface with explicit microphone lifecycle states. Choose user-permitted low latency audio configuration, echo and noise processing only where supported, and a fallback when audio effects worsen the signal. Establish a calibration screen with raw-signal meter and private, local quality feedback; never represent calibration as hardware amplification beyond device capability. Use voice activity detection to determine start/end segments, a tunable silence threshold for quiet speakers, and distinct handling for background noise. Streaming transcription should maintain stable and provisional words, allowing quick corrections without executing commands from unstable partial transcripts. A local wake-word model is optional, subject to battery and policy; tap-to-talk must always work. For voice output, prefer local Android TTS when it meets language requirements; a configured remote TTS engine may improve prosody if privacy/cost is acceptable. Route audio to phone speakers or selected earbuds, independent of desktop audio devices. During speaking, allow tap or permitted barge-in to cancel TTS and start a new request; avoid having the assistant transcribe its own output. Provide clear listening timers, hardware microphone indicators, offline awareness and a single always-visible stop control. Voice-matched identity is a convenience signal, never sufficient for dangerous actions or account authentication.

## System C — Performance and battery economics
Define performance budgets rather than slogans. Track cold start, time to UI interactivity, command parse time, time-to-first partial transcript, time-to-first AI text, time-to-first TTS audio, cross-device command round-trip, p50/p95 latency, memory footprint, dropped animation frames, process death recovery, battery consumed per hour of active voice, and average network bytes per command. Benchmarks must record device, OS version, connection type, model/provider and whether the result was warm or cold. Establish separate profiles: lightweight Redmi 9-class phone, midrange Android, modern flagship, desktop under battery saver, offline LAN, and remote relay. Lazy-load maps, camera, shaders and ML models. Render 3D or particles only when GPU budget allows, always degrade to flat state indicators. Keep command routing local for fast deterministic commands. Compress and coalesce device presence events, avoid needless heartbeats, and cache only user-scoped non-sensitive facts with expiry. Do not ask the OS to keep the screen or CPU awake indefinitely. Monitor UI frame-time and thermal status to reduce effects automatically with an explanation. Performance work must prioritize reliable action results over superficial "instant" visuals that obscure ongoing tool execution.

## System D — Android capabilities and ownership boundaries
Implement Android app launching through documented intents and package visibility configuration. Contacts lookup requires either a scoped picker or runtime contact permission with a clear explanation. Calling a contact should prefer launching the OS dialer or user-approved call route; no auto-dialing ambiguous numbers or simulated conversations. System toggles must use official Android settings panels and permissioned APIs; if a protected setting cannot be changed from third-party apps, show the official settings screen. Notification reading is opt-in via legitimate listener access, with strict data minimization. WorkManager handles deferrable jobs and foreground services are reserved for eligible user-visible tasks. Android 12+ and later background restrictions must be tested on the actual target SDK and OEM devices. Respect scoped storage, package visibility limits, screen-capture restrictions, battery optimization policies, location data accuracy, Bluetooth permission differences, and microphone access indicators. Do not claim control over all apps via AccessibilityService or invent root-only powers. Build per-feature permission state machines including request, grant, deny, revoke, permanently denied, unsupported, and recovery guidance. Keep Android useful even without a connected computer.

## System E — Productivity, studying and personal organization
Build a unified local object model for Task, EventLink, Reminder, Project, Note, DocumentReference, ChecklistItem, ActivitySummary and PlannerProposal. Let users tell J.A.R.V.I.S. "I need to finish my website by Friday" and receive an editable, realistic plan rather than an unwanted calendar write. Calendar connectors must use OAuth or legitimate local event providers, and the app must disclose exactly which calendar it accesses. Task extraction from voice and documents should first create suggestions. For study mode, include step-by-step teaching, explanation of concepts, visual problem understanding, flashcard generation, citations and a learning progress view without fabricating grades or guaranteeing results. Support English, Spanish and Persian educational explanations, time zone handling, 12/24-hour format, accessible quiet mode, and human-friendly reminders. Meeting and email summaries require user-granted sources and explicit privacy boundaries. End-of-day reviews are opt-in, short, supportive and never designed to shame the user for incomplete tasks. Link project context to developer tools and cross-device commands: "Open my study folder on the computer and show the math assignment" routes through an authorized folder adapter and returns a reliable document pointer.

## System F — Personalization with control and explainability
Expose visible user-editable settings for assistant tone, default greeting, response length, wake-word eligibility, language preference, microphone session duration, target desktop, preferred browser, accessibility, animation intensity, quiet hours, chosen skills and tool permissions. Allow separate profiles for Study, Coding, Work, Travel, and Minimal Distraction; require user approval for profile-triggered external actions. Preferences must never overwrite higher-priority safety or operating-system rules. Give a per-setting reset to default. Personal memory should have granular collection toggles, source labels, expiration, export, correction and deletion. Data portability needs a versioned JSON export; portable backup cannot silently include private secrets or credential material. Device context such as which laptop was previously targeted is useful, but it expires and can be overridden instantly by explicit commands. Respect user-specific pronunciations, selected nickname aliases and locale without treating all guesses as permanent identity facts. Do not infer emotional states or medical conditions as facts from voice or engagement patterns. Ensure customization changes actually propagate into the native UI, TTS configuration, voice state machine and backend prompts, not only the settings screen.

## System G — Camera, document understanding, screenshots and visual boundaries
Build a multimodal ingestion pipeline supporting intentional camera capture, image selection, PDF/document picker, and optionally approved desktop screenshot. Each source receives a specific consent receipt and access scope. Use OCR where available, including local models when resource budgets permit, and retain page coordinates or text spans to support references. Image Q&A must distinguish visibly present evidence from assumptions. Privacy-sensitive screenshots may include names, addresses, access tokens, messages or banking details; provide local redaction and explicit cloud-upload approval. The desktop bridge never silently captures the computer display. On Linux use XDG portal approvals for screen-sharing; on macOS honor Screen Recording/Automation permissions; on Windows use supported desktop capture APIs and UI approval. The assistant can tell a user which on-screen button appears relevant but should not infer an app's hidden state from a single screenshot. Keep provenance metadata, data deletion, blur/redaction preview, file-size limits and compression controls. For charts, describe axes and uncertainties, not just numerical trends. For QR codes, preview the decoded destination rather than opening automatically. Avoid making decisions about sensitive personal traits based on images.

## System H — Original holographic visual language and animation engineering
The UI must be recognizably original: charcoal/navy near-black surfaces, cyan/teal light accents, restrained amber for caution, readable typography, and a luminous central orb built from GPU-efficient primitives. Use layered concentric rings, progress arcs, radar sweeps, segmented waveform ribbons, softly orbiting data nodes, purposeful reflections and depth; let the visual state convey functional truth. Listening changes ring pulse and wave responsiveness to microphone activity; thinking shifts to a slower analysis orbit; tool execution displays the target device name and step progress; success displays a short restrained completion flourish; error uses a calm clear warning. Avoid flashing, rapid strobing, sensory overload or battery-hungry continuous 60fps loops while idle. Support reduced motion, high contrast, screen readers, meaningful large touch targets, keyboard traversal, RTL rendering and limited-GPU fallback. Build actual reusable components rather than standalone concept art. Include desktop responsive composition with left navigation rail, center core, right device/task panels and smaller window fallbacks. Screens: Home, Voice, Conversation, Paired Devices, Pairing Wizard, Device Details, Command History, Action Preview, Automation Builder, Skill Library, Memory Manager, Knowledge Sources, Studio, Study, Health & Wellbeing, Calendar, Projects, Files, Vision, Developer Console, Diagnostics, Security, Notifications, AI Providers, Billing/Usage if any, Appearance, Accessibility, Privacy, Help, and Setup. Wire loading, empty, denied, offline, error, success and background transitions for each real feature.

## System I — Privacy, consent, security and store compliance
Protect each user, device and job with authentication, authorization, secure key storage, fine-grained scopes, encryption in transit, data minimization and signed updates. Default to local-only processing where technically feasible and do not falsely label cloud calls as "offline." Pairing QR codes should not contain long-lived secrets. Separate capability grants from physical proximity and user identity. Never bypass OS security controls. No stealth remote administration, silent screen capture, hidden microphone sessions, unlimited file scanning, unauthorized contact sharing, password harvesting, or arbitrary command execution. Treat UI automation as optional and explicitly permissioned; actions to send communications, remove data, publish or deploy software, share locations, or change security settings require matching confirmation levels. Build an audit trail that clearly distinguishes requested, approved, executed, verified and failed actions. Minimize and redact logs. Deletion should cascade across local indexes and backend memory; provide retention period and export. Apply secure update/signing, dependency checks, penetration-testing plan, privacy disclosures and platform-specific store review checklists. For iOS specifically, respect App Intents' foreground/background limitations and do not promise unrestricted system control. For Android, assess foreground-service eligibility. For desktop, be transparent about Accessibility/Automation grants and the risks of those permissions.

## System J — Specialized agents without autonomous overreach
Orchestration should support specialist modules for research, coding, study, organization, documents, UI design, and device management. Each specialist reads only the minimum context needed and emits proposals or typed tool invocations, never raw authority to act. Agent handoffs must have role and task budgets, expiration, error propagation, human approvals for sensitive effects, and a unified progress timeline. Planning must be bounded: a request like "make my website better" should yield a plan, source analysis and edit proposal; repository commits, deployments and paid actions require explicit authorization. Evaluate every agent's citations, test results, input/output schema and task completion; prevent fabricated tool results, unsupported version claims and invisible long-running jobs. Store action receipts and allow cancel/undo where actually possible. A do-it-for-me agent should combine the typed primitives already tested rather than inventing new privileged capabilities. Cross-device targets must be explicit in all agent steps and retained as context only while the approved workflow is active. The user should always be able to see why a desktop app opened, what path was accessed and which permission allowed it.

## System K — Better personal communications
Never automatically send a message just because a language model generated a plausible draft. Contacts resolution should show multiple matches when names collide, including nickname alias mapping controlled by the user. Drafting must support Spanish, English and Persian spelling/RTL. Build previews for SMS, email and compatible notification replies, with delivery status based only on real provider results. Reading email needs a user-authorized connector; notification listener access is not universal access to apps' messages. Call preparation uses selected private notes, while post-call notes must be user-created or consentedly recorded where lawful. Do not record calls silently. Digest logic should filter and group notifications, respect quiet hours and offer user-selected sensitive-content redaction. Encourage clear, respectful social communication rather than manipulative messages. Phone-to-desktop workflows such as "find my meeting notes on the laptop and draft a summary email" must require authorized folder selection and explicit send confirmation. Build spam/phishing previews without reading third-party private data indiscriminately.

## System L — Web information and safe browsing
Live web research, prices, availability and changing policy cannot be accurate without fresh sources. Use legitimate search endpoints or user-requested browser actions. Provide citations and dates; distinguish research summaries from actual browser searches opened on the desktop. Local URL launching should validate scheme, encode the query, and use safe system handlers. Preview suspicious links and prevent automatic navigation to credential-capture destinations when risk indicators are present. A website source can provide facts, but cannot grant Jarvis permission, change system instructions, or authorize sending messages. Track fetch limits, robots/access terms, attribution and user preferences. Save bookmarks and allowed offline snapshots with provenance. Prices and currency rates must include timestamps and currencies; do not guarantee current values from cached data. When no search API is configured, the user can still say "search for X on my computer" and the bridge opens a browser search, but the AI should not claim to have read the search results until it has actually accessed them through an approved mechanism.

## System M — Developer assistance and toolchain workflows
Codex/Claude integrations can inspect code repositories when the user authorizes them and access exists. The app itself must have a working code viewer, structured Logcat/build-error parser, stack-trace interpretation, lint/test harness, and explicit repository write boundaries. Generate a minimal patch with files changed, test status and rollback procedure rather than indiscriminately rewriting modules. No fake "I fixed it" unless tests ran or a verified patch landed. APK extraction cannot reconstruct a full editable app with high reliability, so source repository access is the preferred input. Treat build signing keys, Apple certificates, Microsoft certificates, API tokens and repository credentials as secrets; store them only in secure CI/developer storage. Implement GitHub Actions matrices for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux; iOS builds require macOS-compatible signing/cloud environment. A generic Claude/Codex instruction should ask the agent to examine the repository and choose architecture based on actual source languages, not presume everything is React Native. Provide reproducible commands and honest blockers when credentials or OS runners are missing.

## System N — Creative tools with intellectual-property awareness
Use the assistant to brainstorm, draft, storyboard, edit and organize original creative works, not to clone protected material. A branding module helps compare assets against a user's own guides; a social posting module drafts copy but does not send it without approval. For music, save original user-supplied melodies and provide composition ideas; do not generate unauthorized playback of copyrighted songs. A storyteller produces original narratives with accessible controls, optionally downloadable when licensed. Voice games should work locally when possible, with content filters appropriate to the target user and without compulsive reward mechanics. A presentation coach may assess length, pace and structure from opt-in recordings, but should not demean a user's voice or accent. A visual whiteboard converter performs OCR and diagram extraction from photos chosen by the user. Ensure creators can edit, export and delete outputs, and make it clear when content is synthetic or needs fact-checking.

## System O — Maps, locations, travel and scheduling
Every location feature begins with explicit location consent and a visible explanation of accuracy limitations. Parking memory may store a coordinate at the user's request; it must not claim GPS precision in underground parking. Last-connected accessory positions are historical and not live tracking. Departure predictions require actual travel data; when unavailable, label time estimates as approximate or offer to open the map. Location-based reminders must honor geofence OS limits, power optimization and consent revocation. Travel mode supports offline phrasebooks and editable packing lists, with separately verified live exchange rates. Only trusted contacts selected by the user can receive arrival messages, and a real send requires confirmation. Emergency information tools should never claim guaranteed connection to emergency responders. Test time zones, stale cached maps, device offline, geofences on OEM devices and mixed-language place names. Remember location is sensitive: do not leak it in generic diagnostic reports or proactive messages.

## System P — Experimental AR, interaction and ambient modes
AR overlays and 3D scientific models are experimental, conditional on hardware and SDK support. They should never be critical to essential actions. On the desktop, a high-tech radial HUD is an accessibility-enhancing overlay only when it makes controls simpler, not a reason to obscure real computer apps. Use custom haptics to communicate distinct states; always offer non-vibration equivalents. Lock-screen shortcuts expose minimal private information. The command palette should work with touch, keyboard and voice, presenting actual registered actions sorted by user preference. Offer a timeline of previous actions with receipts rather than an imagined AI memory of what happened. Use original short audio identity cues only where the user has not muted audio; do not play them on the computer when the computer has no audio hardware. For driving use only appropriate hands-free and minimal-distraction functionality, never ask a user to interact with dense UI while driving. Exercise proactive restraint with futuristic effects: clarity, battery health and low-latency functionality take priority.

## System Q — Decision engines, what-if planning and uncertainty management
The assistant should help compare choices through explicit assumptions and constraints rather than pretend to predict the future. A what-if simulator uses user-specified scenarios and describes plausible tradeoffs, not certainty. A contradiction detector compares notes and sources and can ask whether two statements refer to different dates or contexts. A counterexample generator helps find weak points in code and arguments. A complexity estimator describes dependencies, engineering unknowns and risks; it does not promise precise development days without information. A decision matrix should allow adjustable criteria, weights, accessibility and export. In medical, legal, safety-critical or financial decisions, avoid overstated certainty and distinguish educational information from professional evaluation. The user can inspect why J.A.R.V.I.S. ranked one option higher. Training examples must include careful refusal to guess when a critical factor is missing. The result should feel genuinely intelligent precisely because it knows when it lacks evidence.

## System R — Reliability, self-diagnosis and troubleshooting
Construct a diagnostics screen for backend URL configuration, request health endpoint, authenticated ping, model availability, AI request streaming and desktop bridge connectivity. Clearly distinguish 404 route not found, 401 authentication required, 403 denied scope, 429 quota/rate limit, 500 backend error, browser URL open failure, DNS failure, network disconnected, paired device asleep, stale key, permission denied, and unrecognized command. No giant generic "AI not connected" message when a specific fix is known. Capture sanitized logs, correlation IDs, state transitions and independently measured latency. Build a "Test Connection" wizard that does not leak backend keys or user-private messages. Implement support bundle export after explicit review/redaction. Detect duplicate jobs and avoid repeated side effects. In no-key offline mode, diagnostics should explain that browser opening, timers and local commands can still work, while open-domain AI requires model configuration. Make every unsupported feature show a reason and nearest legitimate workaround.

## System S — Health, wellbeing, and humane UX
Here "healthy" means safe for the user's digital wellbeing and device, not an unproven medical treatment system. Include comfortable audio levels, optional reminders to rest eyes and take breaks, quiet hours, screen-time awareness when permissions permit, adjustable screen brightness where supported, low-distraction Focus mode, accessible reading speed, sleep-friendly dim dashboard, and explicit limits on unnecessary notifications. Fitness, nutrition, activity and sleep information can be handled only with opt-in integrations and careful explanation of data uncertainty; do not provide medical diagnoses or body-shaming judgments. For minors, do not promote restrictive eating, overexercise or idealized body standards. Emotional-support language should be respectful, grounded and encourage real-world support when appropriate, not create an exclusive assistant relationship. Emergency features must disclose their non-guaranteed network and system limitations. Provide a Health & Wellbeing screen with user-defined goals, not surveillance-style inferences. No silent health data collection, no manipulative streaks, and no unauthorized sharing of sensitive data.

## System T — Safety gates, delivery truth and auditable release
The project operates across privacy-sensitive devices; correctness means actual functioning code and reliable reporting. Every feature has an owner, status, OS feasibility classification, prerequisite, risk tier, test case, documentation link and manual verification instructions. The primary acceptance path is Android phone voice -> authenticated desktop command -> real OS action -> verified receipt -> phone voice response. Next comes cancellation, revoked access, security tests, and failure-mode clarity. Release gates include licensing, accessibility, crashes, performance on older phones, remote pair revocation, network isolation, private data deletion, dependency scanning, signing, updater verification, clean uninstall and correct model naming. Never claim completion from a static UI. If a feature is blocked by platform policy, implement a compliant alternative and document it. If an API key is not available, keep free local paths useful and show which exact cloud capability is disabled. The final deliverable should be a working staged product with honest progress accounting rather than an overpromised all-in-one APK.

# PART III — DETAILED PRODUCT BUILD CONTRACT, UI FLOWS, AND RELEASE ROADMAP

## 3.1 Audit-first migration rules
Before editing source, inspect the actual repository tree, package managers, build targets, license files, current API usage, OS-specific dependencies, deployment pipelines and test coverage. The project may currently exist as a downloadable APK without source; if source is unavailable, say so and ask for its original app-builder export instead of claiming an APK magically becomes a maintainable application. Identify Kotlin/Compose, Flutter, React Native, Java, web wrappers, backend JavaScript, and any previous code generators. Reuse code when feasible, but do not force cross-platform conversion blindly. Create a compatibility matrix for all 350 IDs across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux with statuses `WORKS`, `PARTIAL`, `PLANNED`, `BLOCKED_OS`, `NEEDS_API`, `NEEDS_PERMISSION`, `NOT_TESTED`. Distinguish platform-side actions from shared backend/model functions. Create a dependency graph; implement thin end-to-end slices before sweeping UI modernization. Preserve working APK functionality with regression tests and avoid massive single-commit rewrites.

## 3.2 The J.A.R.V.I.S. voice-to-desktop demo, step by step
**Milestone One, typed LAN:** Desktop Bridge displays a device pairing QR and direct connection status; Android scans; users compare short verification codes; both save trust keys; mobile offers safe action catalog. Type "Open Chrome and search ChatGPT" in phone; Android maps intent to `OPEN_WEB_SEARCH` with target desktop, safely encoded query and chosen browser; bridge opens the page; status returns to phone. Repeat after restarting bridge. Repeat with browser unavailable and fallback choice. Repeat with a second paired computer and device disambiguation.

**Milestone Two, real microphone:** Android has a conspicuous tap-to-talk button, microphone permission request just in time, listening waveform and actual transcription preview. Speech "Open Chrome on my computer" is parsed to the same intent and reaches the same desktop adapter as typed commands. The phone's TTS speaks the verified receipt. No desktop audio device is ever accessed. Add stop listening, cancel action, punctuation/noise corrections, Spanish/Persian support and turn-by-turn context. Instrument latency.

**Milestone Three, optional wake word:** Evaluate an on-device wake word engine for Android device support and idle battery cost. Expose voice enablement, local privacy indicators and OS-dependent foreground session rules. Don't make indefinite invisible listening a requirement. Implement a timeout-based follow-up window that preserves context and closes recording when expired. Provide hands-free control when allowed, including earbud routes where supported, and a touch mode usable by anyone.

**Milestone Four, OS-specific app integrations:** For Windows use documented app launcher and UI Automation; for macOS NSWorkspace/LaunchServices and optional Accessibility+Apple Events with user approval; for Linux xdg-open/XDG portal and Wayland constraints. Ensure the same high-level command uses OS-specific adapters with equal status semantics, not platform-specific unsafe raw command strings. Disallow dangerous arbitrary shell execution from natural language. File access starts from a desktop-side chooser, not a phone-issued full-disk scan.

**Milestone Five, truly synchronized intelligence:** Add user accounts and approval-based memory sync, selected notes, tasks, device registry, agent progress, and remote relay optional. An assistant question unrelated to the desktop remains functional in phone app even when desktop is offline. A cross-device action when desktop is asleep shows "unavailable" and offers an appropriate scheduled safe retry only if the user opts in. Never fabricate success.

## 3.3 Visual experience by screen and interaction
**Startup screen:** A brief skippable J.A.R.V.I.S. glyph initialization with real permission/backend state. No pretend "100% system access" scan. Optional disable animation. Keep logo small, high resolution and scalable.

**Core/voice screen:** Central radial visualizer with modes `idle`, `ready`, `listening`, `transcribing`, `planning`, `waiting_for_approval`, `executing`, `speaking`, `offline`, `failed`. Users can tap center to talk, tap again to interrupt, hold for typed command drawer, swipe to device hub, and open transcript detail. The design communicates current active input/output without making the user guess. Screen readers receive a text description of every state.

**Device hub:** All paired computers appear with OS icon, friendly name, verified session status, local/cloud connection, latency if measured, permissions, last heartbeat, optional remote relay toggle, selected default, access log and revoke. Pairing wizard offers QR and numeric code. The UI must look premium but have readable buttons and permission descriptions; user can disable cross-device access from either phone or desktop.

**Command console:** A searchable history of actual user commands and receipts, grouped by desktop, with IDs, timings, confirmation stages and failure diagnostics. A "Try again" control checks idempotency and target state rather than blindly repeating destructive actions. Developer mode may expose safe structured JSON with sensitive fields redacted.

**Action preview:** Compact, precise, human-readable: `Target: Windows desktop`, `Action: Open browser`, `Details: Search for "ChatGPT"`, `Permission: Browser launch`, `External effect: browser opens`, `Undo: close browser manually`, `Approve / Cancel`. Higher-risk actions add file names or contact recipients, potential charges and authentication. Only invoke execution after approval when policy requires it. Voice confirmations must read the decisive facts; don't bury them under dramatic sound effects.

**Desktop HUD:** Transparent/dark resizable dashboard with prominent paired phone name, QR pairing, active task, notifications and system-safe actions. Offer small tray/menu-bar mode, full-screen command center, optional always-on-top pane. Animations must be GPU-efficient. The computer app can be completely silent; J.A.R.V.I.S. voice comes from the Android phone. If desktop accessibility is disabled, visually explain which automation actions cannot run and why.

**Memory and privacy:** Separate cards for facts, preferences, projects and devices; search, source trace, edit, expire, delete, export. A microphone activity summary, connection permissions, external actions history, API data settings and encryption indicators live here. Avoid confusing "not synced" with "deleted". Add one-click safety stop, confirmed by a real state transition.

**Developer console:** Show app version, source commit, backend URL health (without secrets), configured models, desktop bridge version, protocol version, STT error types, VAD transitions, command routing, last network errors, authorized folder scopes, active permissions, test harness access and redacted logs. Include a "Why did J.A.R.V.I.S. do that?" view backed by actual proposal, approval, tool and result events, not invented hidden chain-of-thought.

**Health/comfort dashboard:** User-chosen digital wellbeing settings including gentle screen breaks, dim nightstand mode, optional focus blocks, text scaling, hearing-friendly output volume, reduced animation, quiet hours and notifications. No diagnosing, body comparison, streak guilt, or speculative health measurements. Battery thermals can trigger reduction of J.A.R.V.I.S. workload, not an unsupported attempt to kill all other apps.

**Creation/research mode:** Research results show dated sources and citations, imported documents show page references, code mode shows actual files and diff previews, media tools produce original drafts with undo, and cross-device work shows target PC and per-step receipts. All generated content remains user-editable.

## 3.4 Tool design and result states
Every tool declares a stable `tool_id`, version, input/output JSON schema, OS availability, supported user role, requested capability, risk tier, permission scope, confirmation mode, expected side effects, maximum work duration, cost model, cancellation support, offline support, sample success and failure, privacy impact and regression tests. Tool executors never accept extra undocumented fields. Return structured errors with `category`, `code`, `human_explanation`, `retryable`, `needed_permission`, `support_link` and optional sanitized diagnostic trace. Unknown tool names are errors; do not dynamically resolve them as arbitrary filesystem executables. Require explicit feature flags for experimental capabilities and signed manifests for externally installed skills. During a tool call, animate only the state the executor actually reports.

## 3.5 Backend: model and data contracts
The phone's backend URL setting should accept an HTTPS base origin such as `https://project.vercel.app`, derive real `/api/health` and conversation endpoints, and expose a Test Connection button that checks network, TLS, route presence, auth and model provider separately. An HTTP 404 means an endpoint is missing or incorrectly routed, not that the user needs to guess an API key. Client tokens, if used, authenticate sessions and must not impersonate private server credentials. Store provider API keys in backend secret management. Rate limit by user/session, implement streaming and request cancellation, check ownership of memories/documents/projects, maintain versioned migrations, and support deletion and export. Use stable IDs, TTL, source provenance, consent records, encrypted storage where appropriate, and logs without raw chat or microphone data by default. Document what needs cloud network access and what works on LAN. Implement graceful fallback to configured local model where supported and a deterministic command interface when no AI model is available. Validate data from desktop bridge and AI tools as untrusted by default; even an authenticated response must match the expected schema.

## 3.6 Recommended testing matrix
Android: Redmi 9-class budget phone with limited RAM/storage and various available Android versions, an emulator for automated tests, a modern phone for higher-end animation and optional NFC/Bluetooth modes. Do not require all test phones to have sensors they lack. Windows: Windows 11 current supported release, standard user account, no microphone/speaker, browser installed and browser missing, locked desktop, UAC prompt present, user session ended. macOS: an actively maintained supported version with proper Automation/TCC permission scenarios, both Intel/Apple Silicon where build targets require. Linux: one GNOME Wayland distro and one KDE or X11 environment. Network: same LAN, guest LAN isolation, internet unavailable, bridge restart, device asleep, lost Wi-Fi, cloud relay denied. Privacy: each permission denied and revoked while a job is queued; sensitive screenshot redaction; deletion; stolen-phone/unpair revocation; invalid QR; replay attempt; malicious web content. Voice: whispered speech, room noise, Spanish and Persian, phone on table vs near face, earbud routing, TTS interruption, microphone stop. User experience: reduced motion, high contrast, screen readers, localized long text, multi-window desktop, color-blind accessible status differences. No release is ready merely because all unit tests pass; an authenticated real-device end-to-end demo is mandatory.

## 3.7 2027 phased engineering roadmap
**Phase 0 — Inventory and preservation:** Clone actual repository; list every current feature; build Android; locate backend code; document defects and constraints; initialize feature matrix, ADRs, threat model and automated tests. Deliver reproducible baseline and error reproduction for any existing HTTP 404.

**Phase 1 — Backend truth:** Implement real health and chat endpoints, secret management, authenticated sessions, local command classification, error handling, and contract tests. Demonstrate real AI chat only with an actual configured provider or installed local model.

**Phase 2 — Android voice core:** Implement tap-to-talk, STT, text preview, safe intent routing, streaming responses when available, TTS through phone, microphone lifecycle/stop/privacy controls, and multilingual baseline. Benchmark on hardware.

**Phase 3 — Windows bridge MVP:** Create installable visible desktop companion and LAN pairing; implement device ping, app launch, open URL/search and confirmed receipts. Run demo on Windows with no speakers or microphone. Create GitHub Actions Windows installer workflow.

**Phase 4 — macOS and Linux bridge:** Implement compatible local network protocol and adapters for both OSes, user-visible permission onboarding, supported installers, and smoke tests. Avoid blindly transplanting Windows UI automation into other platforms.

**Phase 5 — Reliable paired intelligence:** Add multi-device target selection, reconnect, queues, expiry, status history, global stop, revocation, rule engine, limited automations, typed action previews and safe file grants.

**Phase 6 — Personalization and documents:** Add opt-in memory, project context, selected PDF OCR and Q&A, school tools, scheduled reminders, user-controlled source privacy, sync and export.

**Phase 7 — Model adapters and advanced speech:** Add backend model routing, local model benchmarks, code-switching speech, optional offline wake word, contextual sessions and voice quality test dashboard. Don't claim "perfect" microphone performance.

**Phase 8 — Automation and developer tools:** Build specialized bounded agents, code repository adapters, task planning, developer console, logs, safe command preview, redacted receipts and debuggers.

**Phase 9 — Futuristic interface:** Deliver responsive holographic system on Android and desktop, coherent motion tokens, accessibility, optimized shaders, reduced-motion alternatives, action feedback, app customization and multi-language support.

**Phase 10 — New 50-feature portfolio:** Implement ideas 301–350 by feasibility and impact, including document voice Q&A, legal local backups, NFC/Bluetooth triggers, safe cleaning review, digital wellbeing and skill library. Keep platform-specific limitations explicit.

**Phase 11 — Optional iOS:** If iPhone support remains desired, add a native-installable iOS client with App Intents and approved permissions, testing and signing. It need not provide a privileged replica of Android features.

**Phase 12 — Public beta and release hardening:** Security audit, package signing and notarization, accessibility, privacy policy, API budgets, performance tuning, update channel and staged testing. Publish real installable packages only after verified builds; Apple membership and other store requirements may apply. Export known limitations and statuses.

Each phase must finish with a working vertical slice, changed files, tests actually run, results, detected limits, artifact paths verified in the build environment, and a short next-steps checklist. No fake time estimates, fabricated test screenshots, invented download URLs or ghost backend services.

## 3.8 Training and evaluation set use, not magical model retraining
The 1,000 sample user requests and 2,000 paired example responses below comprise a **test and tuning corpus**. Use it to test language understanding, correct device routing, honest failure messages, tool authorization, confirmation policy, security, responsiveness and tone. They are not a substitute for actual training a foundation model. Store each example with stable ID, domain, normalized intent, tool, risk tier, offline support, pre-execution answer variant and failure-aware answer variant. Split by semantic group so two paraphrases of the same scenario never leak from training into evaluation. Do not embed all examples into every runtime prompt; retrieval or classifier training uses selectively relevant examples. If an actual provider supports fine-tuning, adapt examples to its current official format and verify consent, terms, costs and model compatibility. For local fine-tuning, measure memory/compute needs honestly and preserve a base-model fallback. Evaluate not only exact output string match but tool intent correctness, scope handling, refusal to invent results, end-to-end action success, multilingual transcription accuracy, privacy behaviors, response helpfulness, and graceful offline mode.

Quality gates for training data: deduplicate near-identical utterances, vary accents and paraphrases only with explicit consent, avoid accidentally including real private message text, remove credentials, represent device-unavailable/permission-denied/canceled cases, annotate whether a real action has been executed, add reference responses from actual system receipts, and run versioned regression tests. Maintain a manifest with corpus version, source author, creation date, validation rules and intended uses. Never secretly upload user voice recordings to train models. Two response variants per request are *examples*, not two simultaneous replies. Every assistant response generated by the live app must use the actual current tool state and should not copy a canned success phrase without checking it.

## 3.9 Final requirement to the implementing AI coding assistant
Act as an engineering team, not a storyteller. Inspect the actual repository; do not invent missing source files. Define one stable protocol, build the Android phone as microphone/speaker/control surface, make Windows/macOS/Linux peers that accept only authenticated, scoped, approved commands, and use the optional AI backend for open-domain tasks. Include all 300 original ideas and the additional 50 without duplicating feature IDs. Build the first working demo before adding experimental holograms; then use the design system to improve usability without compromising battery life, accessibility or trust. Document all OS limitations. Train/evaluate intent routing using the supplied example corpus, but never claim to have retrained the model without an actual training pipeline and results. Use the exact phrase "I can't verify that action completed" when a real tool outcome is unknown, not an imaginary success. Every release must be safer, more transparent and more capable than its predecessor.

# PART VI — BASELINE ACCEPTANCE DIRECTIVES RETAINED FROM 15.0

### L. INTEGRATION FLOWS — MAKE THE SYSTEM WORK AS ONE PRODUCT
Implement these end-to-end journeys with source code and screenshots/videos from real builds when your environment allows:

**Journey 1 — First launch and backend repair**: Install -> choose language -> choose local-only or optional cloud account -> request mic only if voice is enabled -> enter backend base URL or use bundled verified production URL -> run `/api/health` -> explain status -> send a real text "What are you?" to configured AI backend -> stream valid response -> speak only if voice enabled. If server returns 404, show the missing route and a documentation link to the expected endpoint; do NOT say vague "AI not connected" with no fix.

**Journey 2 — Wake and call a saved contact**: User starts an authorized voice session -> "Hey JARVIS" -> optional configured greeting -> "Call My Dad" -> local contact resolution from runtime-authorized contacts or contact picker -> match alias -> if multiple matches show chooser -> display name and phone number -> launch ACTION_DIAL or an appropriately permissioned user-initiated call route -> leave actual conversation between humans. The AI should NOT attempt to talk to the recipient or record the call.

**Journey 3 — Fast offline command**: Disconnect internet -> "Open calculator" or tap equivalent -> local command engine classifies -> standard launch intent -> instant success, with no AI-server dependency and no fabricated online result. Display a clear Offline badge only when it conveys actual functionality loss.

**Journey 4 — Intelligent memory**: User explicitly enables memory -> gives a relevant preference -> memory candidate displayed in transparent log/settings -> later asks follow-up in another session -> assistant retrieves relevant fact -> user corrects or deletes it -> next reply no longer uses the deleted fact. Confirm that chat retention and memory retention are independently controlled.

**Journey 5 — Vision and screenshot troubleshooting**: Select screenshot through Share -> detect text/UI -> identify likely button/error -> explain confidence and suggested taps -> never claim control of another app that is not integrated -> if a protected app prevents screenshot capture, explain honestly.

**Journey 6 — Planning and agents**: User says "Create a project plan for my app upgrade" -> coordinator creates scoped subtasks -> specialist agents research/test/plan -> shows source-backed results and a structured plan -> waits for human approval before GitHub write, deployment, messages, or calendar changes -> records a safe execution receipt.

**Journey 7 — Low-end device safe mode**: Detect low performance or power saver -> reduce particles/blur and heavy visuals -> keep text, local commands, essential tasks, and mic controls working -> show a toggle to restore cinematic effects when possible.

**Journey 8 — Privacy and stop**: Disable microphone -> confirm no capture -> revoke notification access -> verify app no longer reads notifications -> delete memories -> verify indexed retrieval exclusion -> press automation emergency stop -> cancel queued work where possible and disclose irreversible operations already completed.

**Journey 9 — Student session**: Capture an exercise image -> verify OCR text -> explain stepwise -> create editable flashcards -> place an approved study reminder -> close without aggressive re-engagement notifications.

**Journey 10 — Developer release**: Import repository -> parse Logcat -> identify issue -> propose minimal fix -> add tests -> run Gradle/backend tests -> confirm API schema -> increment app version appropriately -> generate changelog -> produce signed release build instructions and a Play-ready compliance checklist, without inventing a successful build.

### M. DEVELOPMENT PHASES AND DEPENDENCIES
Work in reproducible vertical slices, preserving app functionality. Do not build 300 isolated mock screens before connecting the backend.

**Phase 0 — Audit and reliable baseline:** inspect existing repo; record current screens; verify Gradle builds and tests; fix base URL/HTTP 404; add real `/api/health` and `/api/assistant/stream`; secure provider keys; wire a functioning question-and-answer round trip. Define compatibility and instrumentation baseline. Output architecture, diff, and pass/fail evidence.

**Phase 1 — Core JARVIS experience:** original animated orb, accessible home, basic device reads, app launch, contact picker/alias matching, call preview, text chat, local commands, permissions, backend diagnostics, error handling, localization foundations. End-to-end call flows verified.

**Phase 2 — Fast reliable voice:** microphone lifecycle, consent, STT/VAD, optional wake word, interruption, TTS streaming, text subtitles, audio routing, offline fallback, low-power support. Verify performance and microphone state on an older physical Android device.

**Phase 3 — Personal intelligence:** chat history, opt-in memory, correction/deletion, context summaries, research sources, document import/OCR, tutor mode, task/calendar, privacy dashboard. Verify no cross-account leakage.

**Phase 4 — Android and productivity:** richer device hub, supported notification integrations, messaging previews, widgets, optional overlay, shortcuts, reminders, files, cloud account OAuth as chosen. Add thorough permission denials and OEM fallbacks.

**Phase 5 — Vision and creative capability:** camera session, image Q&A, OCR, chart interpretation, screenshot help, scan/export, creator tools, source-based comparisons. Validate nonvisual accessibility and battery use.

**Phase 6 — Developer/agent platform:** GitHub, model router, typed tool registry, deterministic policy engine, action previews, sandbox/dry-run, job queue, per-user quotas, team-of-agents UI, mission control and audit history. Never allow AI model text to directly invoke unapproved Android permissions.

**Phase 7 — Futuristic and experimental:** ARCore capability detection, lightweight 3D overlays, wearable companion, optional desktop client, advanced panels, creative visualizations. Keep all experiments behind feature flags and explain device requirements.

**Phase 8 — Hardening and release:** instrument performance, run regression/permission/security/accessibility/localization tests, audit privacy/data deletion, confirm current Google Play API level rules, create screenshots and honest store listing, build a signed AAB where signing materials and environment are available, and publish a complete changelog and known limitations.

**Milestone rule:** At the end of each phase deliver (1) working code, (2) changed file list, (3) test execution results, (4) real device compatibility notes, (5) current feature matrix with statuses, (6) screenshots/recordings if tools support capture, (7) remaining dependencies, (8) next slice. Do not call a feature "finished" based only on a static screenshot.

### N. DATA MODEL, PERMISSIONS, AND OBSERVABILITY
Define database tables or equivalent entities for `User`, `DeviceSession`, `Conversation`, `Message`, `MemoryFact`, `MemorySource`, `Project`, `Task`, `Reminder`, `Document`, `DocumentChunk`, `ContactAlias`, `ActionProposal`, `ActionApproval`, `ActionReceipt`, `Automation`, `AutomationRun`, `ProviderUsage`, `FeatureFlag`, `UserPreference`, `NotificationPreference`, and `AuditEvent`. Define keys, TTL, retention, cascade deletion, migration strategy, and encryption as appropriate. Store consent records, not secret values. Do not store entire phone contacts database in cloud by default.

Document each runtime permission with purpose, screen that requests it, user-visible explanation, whether required/optional, revocation handling, and graceful fallback. In particular include audio recording, contacts, notifications, camera, location, Bluetooth, permitted device settings, foreground services, overlays, and storage picker integrations. Do not request all permissions during onboarding.

Add redacted structured logs with request ID, feature ID, error type, elapsed time, action outcome, privacy risk tier, and model usage. Logs must NEVER contain API keys, access tokens, raw contact phone numbers, full private messages, or raw user images. Telemetry should be opt-in where appropriate and should support full account deletion. Measure battery drain, UI FPS, network request counts, p50/p95 response latency, crash-free sessions, transcription error samples (consented), and backend unit cost.

### O. SECURITY / QUALITY / HEALTHY-UX ACCEPTANCE GATES
Before any release, verify all of the following:
- Build succeeds without private hard-coded credentials, placeholder backend domains, missing imports, or fake API responses.
- `GET /api/health` and `POST /api/assistant/stream` function as documented in production and staging. HTTP 404 and authentication failures have actionable UI.
- Contacts permission can be denied without crashing; contact calls show the correct human and number; the AI does not speak on behalf of the callee.
- Microphone recording occurs only under lawful, user-visible permitted sessions. Stopping or revoking permission genuinely closes audio capture.
- All external messages, account edits, deployments, location shares, and deletions require the correct authorization/confirmation tier.
- Android system restrictions are honored, including notification visibility, background activity/mic restrictions, package visibility, scoped storage, and protected settings.
- Local actions remain useful offline. Cloud-only functions clearly explain why they are unavailable.
- App remains responsive and battery-aware on a Redmi 9-class device, with fallback graphics and manageable storage/memory usage.
- All screens have accessibility labels, readable type, keyboard support where useful, text captions, and reduced-motion settings.
- Translated UI is complete and visually tested in English, Spanish, and Persian RTL.
- Memory opt-in, history deletion, account data export, connection revocation, and automatic retention/TTL work in actual tests.
- Tool prompt-injection tests demonstrate untrusted web/document text cannot override authorization or trigger privileged actions.
- Model pricing/usage caps, quotas, cancellation, and action receipts work under realistic error conditions.
- Test reports, compatibility matrix, known limitations, and user-facing privacy explanations accompany the released artifacts.
- No coercive notifications, invasive personal tracking, pretend emotional dependence, unverified health diagnosis, or misleading feature descriptions.

15. Next prioritized implementation slice if the workspace cannot deliver all 300 at once.

I do NOT want 350 buzzwords, a generic PowerPoint-style strategy, a movie-inspired mockup, or a chatbot interface with buttons that do nothing. I want **J.A.R.V.I.S. v15.1** engineered as a cohesive, modular, inspectable product, with every capability implemented as far as its permissions, hardware, user consent, time, cost, third-party availability, and current Android rules genuinely allow.

**Engineering implementation contract:** Implement this system through On-device capture/detection; ASR provider adapters; custom lexicons and mic quality tools. The AI model must not infer capabilities that do not exist.

# V2 PART H — COMPLETE 1,000-QUESTION / 2,000-ANSWER SCENARIO LIBRARY

These examples are an annex to this single master prompt. Use structured data to load/evaluate them; do not place all examples into a runtime user chat and do not claim these alone fine-tune an AI model. Protect user data, maintain test splits and run real outcome checks.


# PART VII — 1,000 UTTERANCE EXAMPLES AND 2,000 ANSWER EXEMPLARS
Each case contains a user utterance, normalized intent, tool and risk tier, then two alternative pre-execution response patterns. These are not claims that actions already occurred. Split labels can be used for intent-model experiments and regression testing. Never embed the entire catalog in the live context window.

### JQ-0001 — Desktop application control [validation]
**User question / command:** JARVIS, open Chrome on my computer.
**Intent:** `DESKTOP_OPEN_APP` • **Tool:** `desktop.open_app` • **Risk:** 1 • **Offline:** yes
**Answer example A:** I'll request that the paired desktop launch Chrome and confirm only after the bridge replies.
**Answer example B:** I'll check the selected desktop and its launch permission before opening Chrome; if it is unavailable, I'll say so.
**Execution rule:** Examples are pre-action language. Report successful execution only on a valid receipt.

# V2 PART I — DEFINITIVE UX REQUIREMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE WALKTHROUGHS

## I1. All personal assistants are separate, not a shared chatbot

Every Google-authenticated person gets a stable backend user ID, personal memories and preferences, separate conversation history, personal Google service scope grants, own automations, own paired devices and own audio/voice dictionary. On shared family devices, account switch clears or securely isolates caches and visible private history. Add explicit controls for export, disconnection, deletion, consent history and active sessions. Respect organization permissions and any appropriate youth/parental controls of Google services. Do not hard-code a particular person's nickname or email into the shipped app.

## I2. First impression: a clean cinematic welcome screen

On first install, show a quick original cyan/blue central AI core animation with optional sound (muted by default or user-triggered), the headline `WELCOME TO J.A.R.V.I.S.`, subtitle `YOUR INTELLIGENCE. YOUR WORLD. YOUR ASSISTANT.`, and a correctly branded `Continue with Google` control. Make it usable immediately, responsive on older phones, and accessible to reduced-motion/screen-reader users. Explain the purpose of sign-in and data use, include privacy and terms, and allow user-initiated troubleshooting if Google Play services are unavailable. Returning authenticated users should not see a long startup movie. After Google identity verification, present optional service connectors and permissions individually, then enter the existing holographic home. Do not demand all Google scopes to use the app.

## I3. Avatar, system states, status and spoken personality

Maintain the original recognizable J.A.R.V.I.S. AI core, radial HUD, reactive waveform, dashboard cards, voice/text command bar, context panels and native platform controls. Animate distinct real states: idle; wake detected; actively recording; transcribing; uncertain ASR; planning; awaiting approval; tool executing; tool succeeded; partially completed; failed; speaking; offline; privacy disabled. Don't make an 'all systems online' status if the backend or device isn't verified. Add accessible colors/labels, original synthesized voice, profile-selectable tone and fast response streaming. The user can select 'Sir' greetings if desired but can disable formal address.

## I4. Example end-to-end acceptance stories

**STORY 1 — Phone voice operates a PC without PC audio hardware.** Given Android phone and trusted Windows companion on the same permitted network, and no computer microphone or speakers: When user says 'Hey JARVIS, open Chrome on my computer and search for ChatGPT' during supported listening mode, the app transcribes and resolves the device and action, checks authorization, executes desktop.open_app/open_url, verifies browser state from the companion, and speaks confirmation on Android. If the app isn't installed, phone is offline, or permission is denied, it explains the true failure instead.

**STORY 2 — Google sign-in is not full Google data access.** Given an authenticated user without Gmail scope: When they ask 'Read my latest email', J.A.R.V.I.S. says Gmail is not yet connected and offers an official consent flow. If authorization is declined, it stops. If authorized, it fetches only needed data via approved APIs, shows source references, and confirms before any send.

**STORY 3 — Two people, two assistants.** Given user A and B signed in on different devices, A's memory and connected folders cannot be fetched using B's session, forged tool request, or swapped device ID. Account switch removes A data from B view. Security tests must fail closed.

**STORY 4 — Training examples are honest.** Given 1,000 scenario fixtures and 2,000 response examples: The test runner parses all records; knows expected intent/action/risk, runs model evaluation, logs genuine accuracy/latency, and reports which datasets were used for train, validation or test. It never claims that merely adding these examples trained the provider's proprietary foundation model.

**STORY 5 — Safe action on a user's document.** Given two similarly named files and a request to move one: J.A.R.V.I.S. identifies source and target, displays preview, asks confirmation if the action is consequential, moves only the authorized selected file, verifies the destination and offers undo if supported. If uncertain, it asks one clarification, not guesses.

**STORY 6 — Device safety and healthy use.** Given a budget Android phone under resource pressure: Heavy effects fall back to reduced graphics without UI freezing; continuous listening is not secretly enabled; notifications respect quiet hours. Wellbeing features offer breaks, focus support and screen comfort without diagnosis, pressure, body criticism or unhealthy metrics.

**STORY 7 — Cross-platform truthfulness.** Given the same command on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux: The command router selects legitimate OS adapters; missing capabilities return precise limitation and a user-approved alternative. It does not promise to access arbitrary iOS apps or Wayland windows without available system interfaces.

**STORY 8 — Secure APIs and backend error handling.** Given the existing optional client token and secure backend URL settings: A developer can run a health endpoint test, verify HTTP route and method, check auth and schema, distinguish 404/401/403/429/5xx/timeouts and log safe diagnostics. On-device APK never exposes paid API keys. Provide secure server env configuration and CI secrets documentation.

## I5. Quality metrics and release gates

Baseline values must be measured on actual test devices, not invented. Track: onboarding success, auth recovery, API and tool completion success, false-success rate (target zero), cross-account leakage (must be zero), wake-word detection and false triggers, word error rate by language/noise, command intent accuracy, median/95th percentile response latency, frame rate, peak RSS, crash rate, cold start, battery drain per active minute, mobile network traffic, retries, offline fallback coverage, accessibility completion, device pairing reliability, and user interruption success. Set achievable tracked targets after initial profiling; trend them by release.

## I6. Strict Google identity and integration behavior

- Use official Google Sign-In and platform appropriate OAuth 2.0 flows; validate ID tokens server-side and protect PKCE/state as applicable.
- Keep account authentication and Google service permissions completely separate; use granular, incremental authorization and accept partial grants.
- For Workspace/enterprise services, enforce account role, organization policies and admin consent. Some scopes require Google verification and independent security assessment.
- Keep Google account passwords, authentication codes, wallet data, and password-manager secrets entirely outside J.A.R.V.I.S.
- Google Photos uses user-selected media interfaces where required; Google Keep and NotebookLM may not offer the assumed personal account data API; show link or limited capability instead of claiming direct access.
- Google Maps/YouTube/Cloud/Analytics integration must use official supported interfaces and per-service scopes/quotas where available.
- Include a human-readable service catalog, status badge, connection CTA, full disconnect, applicable data erase, and required permissions per service.

## I7. Ship criteria: what must accompany an installer

Provide a versioned source repository, platform build scripts and instructions, verified artifact hashes and signatures if available, uninstall path, app icons and licensing, terms/privacy copy, Google OAuth consent verification guidance, per-platform permission audit, release notes, feature manifest, real test reports, CI logs, and rollback instructions. For APK sideloading, explain legitimate device installation and security warnings without instructing users to disable protection mechanisms. Offer TestFlight/App Store path for iOS and native Windows/macOS/Linux installer paths. Do not invent a ready IPA/EXE or claim a store review is approved before it happens.
